text:
aj: noticing a small spike of 5xxs from eu-west edge after the NAT egress change last night. 503s only for services behind the ALB that do TLS termination.

aj: errors look like TLS handshake resets. logs show 'tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake' from our ingress controller.

sylvia: hmm. did we change anything on ALB listeners or default certs?

aj: no listener config change. we did rotate the NAT gateway to use a new egress pool (port-preserving) and enabled SNAT on the new nodes. regression coincident with that deploy.

mohit: could be SNI being mangled or clienthello truncated by proxy in path. can you grab a tcpdump of clienthello from the ALB side?

aj: grabbing pcaps now. attaching quick excerpt:
```
# tcpdump -n -s0 -w clienthello.pcap 'tcp and port 443'
# tshark -r clienthello.pcap -V | sed -n '1,80p'
Frame 1: ...
    TLSv1.2 Record Layer: Handshake Protocol: Client Hello
        Handshake Protocol: Client Hello
            extension: server_name: host=api-rw-prod.internal
            cipher suites: TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
```

aj: clienthello shows SNI present. but ALB reports different host chosen, and ingress logs show host header is '10.12.5.7' for a short window.

kevin: host header as IP? that smells like NAT translation rewriting source/dest and some middlebox doing HTTP host substitution when doing TLS passthrough/proxying. maybe our egress proxy is intercepting and making a new TLS session to the ALB without preserving Host.

mohit: run openssl s_client from the NAT gateway towards the ALB with -servername to confirm ALB cert selection:
```
openssl s_client -connect alb-eu-west-1:443 -servername api-rw-prod.internal | sed -n '1,20p'
```

aj: ran that from one egress host: ALB returned wildcard prod certificate (expected). but when the traffic comes from the new NAT pool, an intermediate TLS-terminating proxy in the provider path (sigh) is re-establishing TLS and failing to pass SNI through for short flows. it falls back to IP-based host header which makes ingress pick default cert -> handshake fail.

sylvia: do we have traffic shaping or short connection reuse that would trigger that proxy behavior?

aj: yes, our new SNAT pool changed ephemeral port allocation causing many more short-lived source ports, which the upstream provider's SSL proxy optimizes by terminating and re-originating.

kevin: ok two mitigation options: 1) roll back to old SNAT behavior (preserve previous port allocation) or 2) force ALB to use a single default cert that covers the fallback host (riskier), or 3) force TCP passthrough at edge to avoid double-termination.

mohit: short-term: add an ingress rule to accept connections without SNI and map to the correct virtualhost when Host header matches expected host (if provider rewrites Host). hacky but fast.

aj: trying hack: add an ALB listener rule that checks Host header regex for 'api-rw-prod' and pins cert ARN_X even if SNI missing. will monitor.

infra-bot: Deploy started: ingress-rule-add-1976001600 by aj (changes: add Host header regex rule -> cert ARN_X).

kevin: 👍 watch for 503s to drop in the next 5-10m and check for any client call regressions. also let's open a ticket with provider about preserving SNI across their SSL proxy for our NAT pool.

sylvia: follow-up longer-term: prefer egress pool that keeps port mapping and reduces short reconnects. this is also a cost/scale tradeoff for NAT gateway billing.

aj: initial numbers: 503s fell ~80% after rule pushed. provider replied on support channel acknowledging that their proxy does session-termination for high-volume short flows and gave config options for preserving SNI if we keep consistent source ports.

mohit: created incident doc: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/1976001234-sni-nat (will fill RCA).

kevin: thanks all. next steps: ticket with provider, consider egress pool rollback or adjust ephemeral port allocation, and keep the ALB host-rule until provider fixes.

aj: leaving the host-rule in place for now, scheduled rollback window tomorrow if provider config won't be changed. :white_check_mark:
